message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of these reliable sources:

| Source | What it shows | How to use |
|--------|---------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast | Go to <https://www.airnow.gov/> → “Find Air Quality” → type “Los Angeles, CA”. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Global AQI, maps, historical data | Visit <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often embed live AQI widgets | Search “Los Angeles air quality” on their websites. |
| **Mobile apps** (AirVisual, Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | Push notifications, health recommendations | Download from App Store / Google Play and set your location. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, the AirNow website usually updates every 10–15 minutes. Just enter “Los Angeles” and you’ll see the current AQI, the main pollutants, and whether it’s “Good,” “Moderate,” “Unhealthy,” etc.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?" We need to provide current air quality. We don't have real-time data. We can suggest checking AirNow or local sources. We can provide general info. No function needed.
